description: IDENTITY columns (auto-increment with custom start/increment) through the SQL surface: the DESCRIBE TABLE default cell spells the generator (IDENTITY START n INCREMENT m) and the generated values read back with ordered queries. Snowflake guarantees identity values are unique and ascending, NOT gap-free - exact values are asserted only WITHIN one multi-row INSERT (contiguous); across statements the tests pin the seed row and uniqueness (COUNT(*) = COUNT(DISTINCT id)). An explicitly inserted value does not advance the generator, AUTOINCREMENT is the same feature, and the counter persists across intervening queries. Converted 1:1 from features/IdentityTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE test_identity (id INTEGER IDENTITY, name VARCHAR)
DESCRIBE TABLE test_identity
SELECT CONTAINS(MAX(IFF("name" = 'ID', "default", NULL)), 'IDENTITY START 1 INCREMENT 1') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
CREATE TABLE test_identity_custom (id INTEGER IDENTITY(100, 5), name VARCHAR)
DESCRIBE TABLE test_identity_custom
SELECT CONTAINS(MAX(IFF("name" = 'ID', "default", NULL)), 'IDENTITY START 100 INCREMENT 5') FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
CREATE TABLE test_identity (id INTEGER IDENTITY, name VARCHAR)
INSERT INTO test_identity (name) VALUES ('Alice')
INSERT INTO test_identity (name) VALUES ('Bob')
INSERT INTO test_identity (name) VALUES ('Charlie')
SELECT * FROM test_identity
SELECT id, name FROM test_identity ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
SELECT DISTINCT name FROM test_identity WHERE name IN ('Bob', 'Charlie')
SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT id) FROM test_identity
